title: Proxies and Load Balancing Production Review

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a forward proxy from a reverse proxy?
options: A forward proxy is selected for clients; a reverse proxy is placed in front of services
A forward proxy can use TCP, while a reverse proxy can use only HTTP
A forward proxy always terminates TLS, while a reverse proxy never does
A forward proxy distributes database shards, while a reverse proxy stores sessions
questions.explanation: The distinction is who the proxy represents and who places it in the path. A forward proxy acts for clients; a reverse proxy acts as the service-facing entry point.

questions.question: An L7 proxy is configured for TLS pass-through. Which routing input is unavailable to it?
options: Destination port
Connection state
HTTP request path
Source network address
questions.explanation: With pass-through, the HTTP message remains encrypted until the backend. The proxy can use transport metadata, but it cannot inspect the decrypted HTTP path.

questions.question: When may an application treat a forwarded client address as authoritative?
options: Whenever the header contains a public IP address
Only when a trusted edge replaces untrusted values and the receiver verifies the proxy hop
Whenever TLS is enabled somewhere on the path
Only for requests selected by round robin
questions.explanation: Forwarding fields are caller-controlled unless a defined trusted hop strips or replaces them. The receiver must also know which immediate peers are allowed to assert that metadata.

questions.question: Why can least-connections be a poor load signal for multiplexed HTTP/2 traffic?
options: HTTP/2 has no connection state
One connection can carry many concurrent streams with very different backend work
Least-connections disables health checks
HTTP/2 requests cannot be retried
questions.explanation: Connection count no longer tracks outstanding request work closely when many streams share one connection. Active requests, queueing, latency, or application load reports may be more informative.

questions.question: What is the operational difference between readiness and liveness?
options: Readiness decides whether to send traffic; liveness decides whether to restart a stuck process
Readiness encrypts traffic; liveness decrypts it
Readiness selects an algorithm; liveness sets backend weight
There is no difference
questions.explanation: A process can be alive but unable to serve its full request contract. Readiness removes it from serving, while liveness is about restarting a process that cannot recover in place.

questions.question: Four backends each handle 600 RPS, split two per zone. If one zone fails while clients send 1,600 RPS, what is the capacity shortfall before retries?
options: 0 RPS
200 RPS
400 RPS
questions.explanation: The surviving zone has 2 x 600 = 1,200 RPS of capacity. Client demand is 1,600 RPS, so the shortfall is 400 RPS before any retry amplification.

questions.question: Why is a proxy timeout not proof that retrying a POST is safe?
options: The first request may have committed after the proxy stopped waiting
POST requests cannot carry an idempotency key
A timeout always means the backend was never selected
The proxy converts the retry into a TCP health check
questions.explanation: A timeout leaves the durable outcome uncertain. The application must recognize the same logical operation and return its original outcome, or the retry can repeat the business effect.

questions.question: Which rollout evidence best supports promoting a load-balancer configuration?
options: The configuration file parsed successfully
The proxy process stayed alive for one minute
A canary preserved route, identity, retry, health, latency, and saturation guardrails under representative traffic
Every backend received exactly the same number of TCP connections
questions.explanation: Syntax and process health are necessary but incomplete. Promotion needs user-visible and backend evidence that the candidate preserves the complete traffic contract.
